hero.title: Sunday polo on *historic Whitney Field*
hero.lede: Matches open to the public every Sunday in spring and fall, at 2 and 3:30 pm, in the heart of Aiken’s historic horse district. General admission is $10, and parking in the sand lot is free.

sections.title: Your Sunday *at the polo*
sections.intro: Games usually last an hour and a half to two hours. Check the hotline, (803) 643-3611, before heading to the field, especially when it’s wet or the weather looks threatening.

items.name: General admission
items.desc: Free parking in the sand lot next to the field

sections.footnote: In 2025 the pavilion was catered by Park Avenue Oyster Bar and The Willcox. The horses can jump the boards during play, so stay 15 feet back from them.

sections.title: Where American polo *wintered*
body: Polo arrived in Aiken in 1882, just six years after the game reached this side of the Atlantic. It became part of Winter Colony life, drawing many of the best players in the country and the world, and by World War II Aiken was the center of American polo in the winter months.

Today Aiken has an international reputation as a place to play, and to breed and train polo ponies. Players come for the spring season on their way north from Florida and for the fall on their way south, and more of them now stay all year.

items.desc: Practices Wednesday and Friday afternoons and Sunday mornings, two pavilion wristbands, and $500 off one tournament entry per team

sections.footnote: Pop-up tents, tables and chairs are welcome at field-side spots.

items.title: Tiger Kneece, polo manager
items.text: A former 7-goal professional who runs practices and tournaments and coaches Aiken Youth Polo. (803) 646-3301.

items.title: Susie Kneece, marketing
items.text: Sponsorships, advertising in the Aiken Polo Magazine, annual parking and club questions. (803) 295-8971.

items.title: Charlie Bostwick, president
items.text: Grew up playing on Aiken’s fields; his father, Hall of Fame player Pete Bostwick, started playing at the club in the 1930s.

items.a: Call the polo hotline, (803) 643-3611, before you head to the field. Matches can change when it’s wet or the weather looks threatening.

items.q: How long does a match last?
items.a: Usually an hour and a half to two hours. There are two matches each Sunday, at 2 and 3:30 pm.
The sand lot next to the field on Mead Avenue is free. Field-side spots are $50 per car, and there are only a few.
